newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real drops 0.02 percent on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real drops 0.02 percent on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.02 percent on Tuesday to close at 1.0582 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market, with the currency partially weakened by a fresh cut in the reais/dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The central bank lowered the mini-band by 0.05 percent to between 1.0580 and 1.0630 reais per dollar through a buy/sell auction in mid-morning.

Dealers said the move by the bank fulfilled market expectations. The forex market had expected a cut of at least 0.1 percent on Monday but the central bank lowered it by just 0.05 percent to between 1.0575 and 1.0625 reais per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.09 percent. During the last few months, the bank has lowered the mini-band by between 0.5 and 0.6 percent each month.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.02 percent to end at 1.0642 per dollar. In the parallel market, the real closed flat at 1.130 per dollar.
